flows.what: an optimized kernel/module implementation to inject
served through the unmodified HuggingFace Transformers interface

content.key_idea: KTransformers sits as a drop-in engine beneath the standard HuggingFace Transformers interface, injecting hardware-specific optimized modules (fused-MoE, AMX/AVX-512, FlashInfer, Marlin kernels) to replace default PyTorch modules across heterogeneous CPU/GPU hardware, for any supported MoE model, with no user-facing API changes.
content.reading_order: Center-out: a generic module-injection/kernel-replacement graph inside the purple KTransformers box, flanked left by pluggable MoE Models and right by Advanced Operators, sandwiched between the User Interface band above and Heterogeneous Hardware band below.

light tan background of the User Interface and Heterogeneous Hardware bands

style.stroke: medium (~1.2pt) solid dark borders on all boxes and bands, no dashing
style.font: Calibri sans-serif, about 6.5pt body text, bold and larger (~11pt) for band and system titles
style.corners: mixed: rounded pill-shaped boxes for model/kernel/hardware items, square bands for the four surrounding panels
style.arrows: thick white block/chevron arrows connecting the four flanking panels to the central KTransformers box, plus one small right-arrow inside the box showing the before/after graph transformation
style.icons: vector, small computation-graph (nodes/edges) icon showing a generic module graph transformed into one with three highlighted nodes

encoding.color_means: purple = the KTransformers system itself (title, borders, injected-optimization box outlines); light gray = swappable upstream/downstream option lists (MoE Models, Advanced Operators); light tan = the interface and hardware boundary bands; colored graph nodes = specific modules replaced/optimized inside the generic computation graph
encoding.emphasis: large white block arrows on all four sides funnel every external resource (models, operators, hardware, interface) into or out of the single purple KTransformers box, making it the unmistakable center of the architecture
reusable_patterns: central engine box flanked by two option-list sidebars and sandwiched between an interface band and a hardware band
before/after generic computation-graph icon to depict a module-injection/kernel-replacement transformation
weaknesses: the mapping between the three colored nodes in the after-graph and the three named optimization boxes (Module Injection, Kernel Replacement, Overhead Reduction) is implied only by adjacency and color, not labeled explicitly

evidence: KTransformers extends a standard HuggingFace Transformers implementation
allowing a flexible injection of optimized implementations tailored for specific hardware to replace default PyTorch modules
KTransformers retains full compatibility with the widely-used HuggingFace interface, requiring no end-user changes

summary: KTransformers is a high-performance inference engine for heterogeneous CPU/GPU execution of large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models such as DeepSeek, extending standard HuggingFace Transformers so end users need no code changes. Figure 5 draws it as a purple core box sandwiched between a tan 'User Interface' band on top (HuggingFace Transformers) and a tan 'Heterogeneous Hardware' band below (Intel Xeon CPUs, Nvidia A100/RTX 4080 GPUs), connected by large white block arrows. Gray sidebars flank the core: 'MoE Models' on the left (DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, Mixtral, Kimi) feed in, and 'Advanced Operators' on the right (Fused-MoE Module, AMX/AVX-512 kernels, FlashInfer Module, Marlin Kernel) feed into a 'Kernel Replacement' box. Inside the core, a small before/after computation-graph icon with three labeled boxes (Module Injection, Kernel Replacement, Overhead Reduction) depicts swapping default PyTorch modules for optimized ones.

notes: layout-proposal: flanked-core - a central engine box (KTransformers) is sandwiched between a top interface band and bottom hardware band linked by large block arrows, while two side sidebars of swappable model/operator options feed horizontally into the same core, forming a plus-shaped composition.
